name: Texas Pacific Land

logo.source: texaspacific.com site header logo PNG (536x148); Wikipedia has no infobox logo for TPL

description: Texas Pacific Land owns about 894,000 surface acres, mostly in the Permian Basin of West Texas, and about 224,000 net royalty acres. It does not drill. Oil and gas companies pay it a royalty on production from its acres, pay for easements to run pipelines and power lines across the land, and buy brackish water and pay per barrel to dispose of produced water on its land. It also sells land and construction materials such as caliche and sand. Revenue was $798 million in 2025 with a net income of $481 million, and about three quarters of it was operating income. Its royalty interests require no capital spending or operating cost for well development (10-K). It has begun selling and buying land tied to data-center and power projects.

gics.industry: Oil & Gas Exploration & Production (to be verified)
gics.note: Conventional GICS label recorded from general knowledge of the standard scheme; not re-checked against an MSCI/S&P source in this pass. SEC SIC 6792 (Oil Royalty Traders). TPL states "We are not an oil and gas producer": it owns land and royalty rights and bears no drilling or operating cost, and 48% of 2025 revenue was not oil and gas royalties (water, easements and land). It has about 114 employees.

hq.note: 2699 Howell Street, Suite 800 (FY2025 10-K cover); Delaware corporation

employees.note: 114 full-time employees, 35 of them at the water subsidiary TPWR (FY2025 10-K)

businessLines.name: Land and Resource Management
businessLines.how: Royalty: a share of the value of oil, gas and NGLs the operators produce from wells on TPL's acres, paid monthly, with no cost to TPL, so it follows commodity prices and drilling pace (TPL says it is exposed to operator decisions). Easements: one-off payments for pipeline and power line rights, renewing every 10 years with CPI-linked resets. Land sales: occasional, lumpy sales of parcels.
businessLines.description: Oil and gas royalties, easements and other surface-related income (pipelines, power lines, commercial leases, material sales), and land sales, on about 882,000 surface acres (894,000 at June 30, 2026) and 224,000 net royalty acres.

businessLines.name: Water Services and Operations (TPWR)
businessLines.how: Operators pay per barrel for brackish water delivered for drilling and completion, and pay a royalty per barrel when a third party disposes of produced (wastewater) water on TPL land; revenue tracks the volume of wells drilled and fracked and of water produced with oil.
businessLines.description: Sourcing and selling brackish water for oil and gas operations, and receiving royalties on produced water handled on TPL land.

brands.name: Texas Pacific Water Resources (TPWR)
brands.share: 38.5% of FY2025 revenue and 33.4% of FY2025 operating income (share of the two segments' $592.2M)

whatsNext.text: Chevron Project Kilby (Reeves County power plant supporting a data center): TPL sold land for $42.5M and got the exclusive right to supply aquifer water; payment is a nominal cash amount at closing plus annual payments through 2046, with a put/call option if development milestones are missed
Data-center and power generation initiative: $50.0M minority investment in Bolt Data & Energy (Dec 2025) plus land bought in Shackelford and Jones counties in 2026
